text:
Shown in the figure is a hollow icecream cone (it is open at the top). If its mass is M, radius of its
top, R and height, H, then its moment of inertia about its axis is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The curved surface carries mass $M$ spread uniformly over its area $πRL$, where $L=\sqrt{R^{2}+H^{2}}$ is the slant height, so $σ=\dfrac{M}{πRL}$.

A circular strip at slant distance $s$ from the vertex has radius $r=\dfrac{sR}{L}$ and width $ds=\dfrac{L}{R}dr$, so its mass is

$dm=σ(2πr)ds=\dfrac{M}{πRL}\cdot 2πr\cdot \dfrac{L}{R}dr=\dfrac{2M}{R^{2}}rdr$

This is the same distribution of mass with distance from the axis as in a uniform disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$: pressing the cone flat along its axis moves no element closer to or farther from the axis.


[IMG]

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{R}r^{2}dm=\dfrac{2M}{R^{2}}\int\limits _{0}^{R}r^{3}dr=\dfrac{MR^{2}}{2}$

The mass is spread from $r=0$ to $r=R$, not concentrated at $R$ as in a ring, and $H$ does not enter.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

$L_{i}$
 $= L_{f}$

$r_{\min }v_{\max } = r_{\max }v_{\min } .....(i)$

Given, $v_{\max } = 6v_{\min }$

From equation (i),

$\frac{r_{\min }}{r_{\max }}$ = $\frac{v_{\min }}{v_{\max }}=\frac{1}{6}$

text:
You are given that Mass of ${}_{3}^{7}Li$ = 7.0160u,

Mass of ${}_{2}^{4}He$ = 4.0026u

and Mass of ${}_{1}^{1}H$ = 1.0079u.

When 20 g of ${}_{3}^{7}Li$ is converted into ${}_{2}^{4}He$ by proton capture, the energy liberated, (in kWh), is :

[Mass of nucleon = 1 GeV$/c^{2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
${}_{3}^{7}Li$ + ${}_{1}^{1}H$ $\to$ 2(${}_{2}^{4}He$)

$\Delta$m = $[M_{Li}+M_{H}]-2[M_{He}]$

= (7.0160 + 1.0079) - 2 $\times$ 4.0003

= 0.0187

Energy released in 1 reaction = $\Deltamc^{2}$

In use of 7.016 u Li energy is $\Deltamc^{2}$.

In use of 1 gm Li energy is $\frac{\Delta mc^{2}}{m_{Li}}$.

In use of 20 gm energy is = $\frac{\Delta mc^{2}}{m_{Li}}\times 20$

= $\frac{0.087\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 10^{9}}{7.016\times 1.6\times 10^{-24}}\times 20$ J

= 0.05 $\times$ $10^{14} J$

= 1.33 $\times$ $10^{6}$ kWh
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

text:
If the potential energy between two molecules is given by

U = $-\frac{A}{r^{6}}+\frac{B}{r^{12}}$,

then at equilibrium,
separation between molecules, and the potential energy are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
U = $-\frac{A}{r^{6}}+\frac{B}{r^{12}}$

F = - $\frac{dU}{dr}$

$= – (A(–6r^{–7}$
$)) + B(–12r^{–13})$

for equilibrium, F = 0

$\therefore$ 0 = $\frac{6A}{r^{7}}-\frac{12B}{r^{13}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{6A}{12B}=\frac{1}{r^{6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ r = $\left (\frac{2B}{A}\right )^{\frac{1}{6}}$

$\therefore$ U = $-\frac{A}{\frac{2B}{A}}+\frac{B}{\left (\frac{2B}{A}\right )^{2}}$

= $-\frac{A^{2}}{2B}+\frac{A^{2}}{4B}$

= $-\frac{A^{2}}{4B}$

text:
An electron is moving along +x direction with a velocity of 6 $\times$ $10^{6}$
 $ms^{–1}$. It enters a region of uniform
electric field of 300 V/cm pointing along +y direction. The magnitude and direction of the magnetic
field set up in this region such that the electron keeps moving along the x direction will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\vec{B}$ must be in +z axis.

$\vec{V}=6\times 10^{6}\hat{i}$

$\vec{E}=300\hat{j}$ V/cm = 3 $\times$ $10^{4}$ $\hat{j}$ V/m

$\vec{F}$ = $q\vec{E}+q\vec{V}\times \vec{B}$

$\therefore$ $q\vec{E}+q\vec{V}\times \vec{B}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$qE = qVB

$\Rightarrow$ B = $\frac{E}{V}$ = $\frac{3\times 10^{4}}{6\times 10^{6}}$ = 5 $\times$ $10^{–3} T$

text:
In the figure below, P and Q are two equally intense coherent sources emitting radiation of
wavelength 20 m. The separation between P and Q is 5 m and the phase of P is ahead of that of Q
by $90^{o}. A, B$ and C are three distinct points of observation, each equidistant from the midpoint of
PQ. The intensities of radiation at A, B, C will be in the ratio :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the distace of each point from midpoint = d

For point A :

$x_{P} – x_{Q} = (d + 2.5) – (d – 2.5) = 5 m$

$\Delta𝜙$ due to path difference = $\frac{2π}{λ}(\Delta x)$ = $\frac{2π}{20}(5)$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

At A, Q is ahead of P by path, as wave emitted by Q reaches before wave emitted by P.

Total phase difference at A 

= $\frac{π}{2}-\frac{π}{2}$ (due to P being ahead of Q by 90º) = 0

$\therefore$ $I_{A} = I_{1} + I_{2} +$ $2\sqrt{I_{1}}\sqrt{I_{2}}$ cos $\Delta𝜙$

= I + I + $2\sqrt{I}\sqrt{I}\cos (0)$

= 4I

For point C :

$x_{Q} – x_{P} = (d + 2.5) – (d – 2.5) = 5 m$

$\Delta𝜙$ due to path difference = $\frac{2π}{λ}(\Delta x)$ = $\frac{2π}{20}(5)$ = $\frac{π}{2}$

Total phase difference at C = $\frac{π}{2}+\frac{π}{2}$ = $π$

$\therefore$ $I_{C} = I_{1} + I_{2} +$ $2\sqrt{I_{1}}\sqrt{I_{2}}$ cos $\Delta𝜙$

= I + I + $2\sqrt{I}\sqrt{I}\cos (π)$

= 0

For point B :

$x_{P} – x_{Q} = 0$

$\Delta𝜙$ due to path difference = 0

$\Delta𝜙$ = $\frac{π}{2}$ (Due to P being ahead of Q by 90º)

$\therefore$ $I_{B} = I_{1} + I_{2} +$ $2\sqrt{I_{1}}\sqrt{I_{2}}$ cos $\Delta𝜙$

= I + I + $2\sqrt{I}\sqrt{I}\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )$

= 2I

$I_{A}$ : $I_{B}$ : $I_{C} = 4I$ : 2I : 0

= 2 : 1 : 0
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Object is at 2f. So image will also be at $2f. (I_{1})$.

Image$(I_{2})$ of $I_{1}$ will be 1 m behind mirror.

Now $I_{2}$ will be object for lens.

$\therefore$ u = -3 m

f = + 0.5 m

$\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{u}$

= $\frac{1}{0.5}+\frac{1}{-3}$

$\Rightarrow$ v = $\frac{3}{5}$ = 0.6 m

So total distance from mirror = 2 + 0.6 = 2.6 m and real image.

text:
A particle of charge q and mass m is moving with a velocity $-v\hat{i}$ (v $\neq$ 0) towards a large screen
placed in the Y - Z plane at a distance d. If there is a magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_{0}\widehat{k}$
, the maximum value of v
for which the particle will not hit the screen is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In uniform magnetic field particle moves in a circular path, if the radius of the circular path is 'd', particle will

r = $\frac{mv}{qB_{0}}$

To not collide, r < d

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{mv}{qB_{0}}$ < d

$\Rightarrow$ v < $\frac{qB_{0}d}{m}$

$\therefore$ $v_{\max } =$ $\frac{qB_{0}d}{m}$

text:
The density of a solid metal sphere is determined by measuring its mass and its diameter. The
maximum error in the density of the sphere is $\left (\frac{x}{100}\right )$ %.  If the relative errors in measuring the mass
and the diameter are 6.0% and 1.5% respectively, the value of $x is_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ρ$ = $\frac{M}{V}$ = $\frac{M}{\frac{4}{3}π\left (\frac{D}{2}\right )^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ρ$ = $\frac{6}{π}MD^{-3}$

For maximum error

$\frac{dρ}{ρ}\times 100=\frac{dM}{M}\times 100+3\frac{dD}{D}\times 100$

= 6 + 3 $\times$ 1.5

= 10.5 %

= $\left (\frac{1050}{100}\right )$ %

$\therefore$ x = 1050

text:
Initially a gas of diatomic molecules is contained in a cylinder of volume $V_{1}$
 at a pressure $P_{1}$
 and
temperature 250 K. Assuming that 25% of the molecules get dissociated causing a change in
number of moles. The pressure of the resulting gas at temperature 2000 K, when contained in a
volume $2V_{1}$
 is given by $P_{2}$
. The ratio $\frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}$
 is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initially $n$ moles of diatomic molecules occupy volume $V_{1}$ at pressure $P_{1}$ and $250\text{K}$:

$P_{1}V_{1}=nR(250)$

When 25% of the molecules dissociate, $\dfrac{n}{4}$ moles of molecules break up and each molecule gives two atoms, producing $\dfrac{n}{2}$ moles of atoms, while $\dfrac{3n}{4}$ moles of molecules remain. The total amount becomes

$\dfrac{3n}{4}+\dfrac{n}{2}=\dfrac{5n}{4}$

In the final state at $2000\text{K}$ in volume $2V_{1}$:

$P_{2}(2V_{1})=\dfrac{5n}{4}R(2000)$

Dividing the two equations,

$\dfrac{2P_{2}}{P_{1}}=\dfrac{5}{4}\times \dfrac{2000}{250}=10\Rightarrow \dfrac{P_{2}}{P_{1}}=5$

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Morning Slot
